clue.text: Artificial colouring (white) put in most of the food!

definitions.text: Artificial colouring (white) put in most of the food!

parts.words: Artificial colouring (white) put in most of the food!
parts.note: the white artificial things are dentures, which are put into the mouth whenever most food is eaten

explanation.surface: A complaint about white food dye added to nearly everything we eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are artificial, white, and go in for nearly every meal, which the clue dresses up as a food additive.

clue.text: Remains at work in the lumber-mill…

definitions.text: Remains at work in the lumber-mill…

parts.words: Remains at work in the lumber-mill…
parts.note: the fine debris left after timber is cut, the remains of a saw's work

explanation.surface: Someone stays on working at the timber mill.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine wood particles are what remains when timber is cut at a mill.

clue.text: … Getting this hard work done

definitions.text: … Getting this hard work done

parts.note: hard work, such as the sawing of the previous clue, leaves one weary

explanation.surface: Finishing a demanding job.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard labour leaves one weary and worn out.

clue.text: Bouquet of flowers!

definitions.text: Bouquet of flowers!

parts.note: bouquet can mean a pleasant smell rather than a bunch

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers given as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet in the sense of a sweet smell, such as flowers give off.

clue.text: She won't be allowed out to play if her character's bad!

definitions.text: She won't be allowed out to play if her character's bad!

parts.words: She won't be allowed out to play if her character's bad!
parts.note: a female stage performer gets no role if she plays her part poorly

explanation.surface: A naughty girl is kept in as a punishment for bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A female performer who portrays characters on stage or screen.

clue.text: Bank will want the money for big loan to be tied up

definitions.text: Bank will want the money for big loan to be tied up

parts.words: Bank will want the money for big loan to be tied up
parts.note: a lender wants a large loan backed by collateral, and also means fastened

explanation.surface: A bank wants assurances before lending a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A loan backed by property is guaranteed, and the word also means fastened or tied.

clue.text: He walks out of a permanent job

definitions.text: He walks out of a permanent job

parts.words: He walks out of a permanent job
parts.note: a vagrant walks the roads as a constant way of life, with no work

explanation.surface: A worker quits a secure post.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant who walks from place to place, permanently without work.

clue.text: C in C, Crete, circulates description of one a bit peculiar

definitions.text: description of one a bit peculiar

indicators.note: something that circulates goes round and round, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief tours Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: C in C is the usual short form of commander-in-chief; 'circulates' mixes C, IN, C and CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slightly odd is described as unconventional or quirky, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Lady guest, getting her invitation

definitions.text: Lady guest, getting her invitation

parts.note: a guest receives an invitation from the woman holding the party

explanation.surface: A woman receives an invitation to a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman who invites and entertains guests at a party.

clue.text: Guarantee to promote a sergeant, for instance

definitions.text: Guarantee
to promote a sergeant, for instance
definitions.meaning: a senior non-commissioned officer may be raised to a rank held by official document rather than commission

explanation.surface: A promise that a sergeant will be promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a guarantee, and also names the army rank above sergeant held by such a document.

clue.text: Take them, in place of a casino owner

definitions.text: Take them, in place of a casino owner

parts.words: Take them, in place of a casino owner
parts.note: gamblers take risks, and a casino is a house of games of luck

explanation.surface: A gambler is urged to take a risk at the house's expense.
explanation.definitionFit: One takes risks of this kind, and a casino deals in them for its owner.

clue.text: Women appear overdressed, wearing such clothes!

definitions.text: Women appear overdressed, wearing such clothes!

parts.words: Women appear overdressed, wearing such clothes!
parts.note: items worn beneath outer garments, so the wearer is literally dressed over them

explanation.surface: A remark that women look overdressed in certain outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments worn beneath the others leave the wearer literally dressed over, so overdressed in a pun.

clue.text: Collected together twenty four old shilling coins

definitions.text: Collected together twenty four old shilling coins

parts.words: Collected together twenty four old shilling coins
parts.note: in pre-decimal British money twelve small coins made a shilling, so two shillings held twenty-four of them

explanation.surface: A collector gathers two dozen old British coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1971 British money had twelve pennies to the shilling.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the old British small coins, plural of penny, twelve to a shilling.

clue.text: Seats for a Royal Command Performance?

definitions.text: Seats for a Royal Command Performance?

parts.words: Seats for a Royal Command Performance?
parts.note: royal seats are the chairs of state from which monarchs command; a Royal Command Performance is a British variety show attended by royalty

explanation.surface: Booking seats for the annual royal variety show in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Command Performance is a yearly British variety show before the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceremonial chairs used by kings and queens are the seats from which royal commands are given.

clue.text: Wants moderate to call one this? Assuredly not!

definitions.text: Wants moderate to call one this? Assuredly not!

parts.words: Wants moderate to call one this? Assuredly not!
parts.note: one with moderate wants is the opposite of greedy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether moderation earns a certain label.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping and greedy, the opposite of having moderate wants.

clue.text: Call it quits!

definitions.text: Call it quits!

parts.note: to give up and leave the scene is to go off

explanation.surface: Someone decides to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: One who calls it quits leaves or goes away, which is what this verb describes.

clue.text: Has nothing to do with regular income

definitions.text: Has nothing to do with regular income

parts.words: Has nothing to do with regular income
parts.note: a retired person has no work but receives a regular state payment

explanation.surface: A remark that something is unrelated to a steady salary.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person draws a regular allowance while having no work to do.

clue.text: Train one to race

definitions.text: Train one to race

parts.note: a fast train that runs without many stops races along

explanation.surface: Coaching someone to run.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast non-stopping train is called by this name, so it is a train made to race.

clue.text: Marks off what one's done!

definitions.text: Marks off what one's done!

parts.note: having one's marks rubbed off means being wiped out

explanation.surface: Ticking off completed tasks on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbed out or erased, so marks have been taken off.

clue.text: Has a duty to Royal Academy, being taught in it

definitions.text: Has a duty to Royal Academy
definitions.meaning: one owing allegiance to a monarch is a citizen of the crown

definitions.text: being taught in it
definitions.meaning: a topic or discipline studied at an academy

explanation.surface: Someone owes duty to an art academy and studies there.
explanation.definitionFit: A person owing allegiance to a monarch, and also a topic studied at school.

clue.text: Damn' EEC regulation posed a threat to me!

definitions.text: posed a threat to

indicators.note: the European Economic Community issued regulations, and regulation here rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: A grumble that a European Economic Community rule threatened me.
explanation.definitionFit: To threaten someone is to put them in danger, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Divine the author of this work.", Contrary to Natural Law"

definitions.text: Divine the author of this work.", Contrary to Natural Law"

parts.words: Divine the author of this work.", Contrary to Natural Law"
parts.note: an event beyond natural law is credited to God as its author

explanation.surface: A request to guess who wrote a book titled Contrary to Natural Law.
explanation.definitionFit: A wonder that defies natural law is attributed to a divine author.

clue.text: Needed quiet sort of place for high diver

definitions.text: place for high diver

indicators.note: to sort letters is to rearrange them

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A high diver needed a calm spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The deepest part of a swimming pool is where divers from the high board land.

clue.text: Broken-down cafe has tip-top view

definitions.text: view

indicators.note: something broken down is in pieces, so the letters of cafe are rearranged
the tip of the word top is its first letter

explanation.surface: A dilapidated cafe nevertheless enjoys a splendid view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken-down' rearranges CAFE into FACE; 'tip' takes T from top.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect or side of something is one particular view of it.

clue.text: Crossing the road to stop people passing by

definitions.text: Crossing the road to stop people passing by

parts.words: Crossing the road to stop people passing by
parts.note: an obstruction placed across a street prevents anyone going past

explanation.surface: Pedestrians crossing a road to avoid passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrier built across a street keeps people from passing through.

clue.text: Group of bees, etc

clue.text: Making one factory owner bankrupt, maybe

definitions.text: Making one factory owner bankrupt, maybe

parts.words: Making one factory owner bankrupt, maybe
parts.note: a factory shutting down could well ruin its owner

explanation.surface: A factory owner faces ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutting down of a works may leave its owner bankrupt.

clue.text: Limit study to judicial punishment

definitions.text: Limit

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a money penalty imposed by a court

explanation.surface: Restricting study as a punishment handed out by a court.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict something is to keep it within bounds, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Cast down as a result of being floored, so to speak?

definitions.text: Cast down as a result of being floored, so to speak?

parts.words: Cast down as a result of being floored, so to speak?
parts.note: to be floored is to be knocked flat, and hopes thrown down utterly are ruined

explanation.surface: Someone depressed after being knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to ruin hopes completely, literally throwing something onto the floor.
